sourceFitAssessment.learnerTask: Distinguish single-site affinity, multiple-contact avidity and a reachable epitope.
sourceFitAssessment.gap: The grip analogy and assay table do not show multiple contacts or an inaccessible native binding site.
sourceFitAssessment.accuracyGuardrails: Separate single-site affinity, multivalent avidity and native epitope accessibility. Stronger binding in one assay does not prove better delivery, specificity, developability or clinical benefit.
sourceFitAssessment.reasoning: The same schematic binding shape makes one individual contact, two linked contacts at nearby membrane targets, and fails to access an occluded site. Affinity is defined under one-to-one conditions, avidity depends on geometry/reconnection, and native access remains a separate test. Neither the schematic nor its caption promotes higher affinity to better tumor delivery or clinical benefit; stability and unwanted recognition remain separate. The fictional A/B example correctly identifies 1 nM as tighter than 10 nM under the same single-site assay while declining a treatment ranking. No physical scale, experimental yield or outcome quantity is encoded in the drawing.
